title: Types of Sharks
desc: Fifty-six kinds of sharks, picture and name first — great white, hammerhead, whale shark and more. A facts deck (one true fact per shark) waits as Stage 2, ready to turn on later.

cards.name: Great White Shark
cards.def: It has about 300 sharp teeth, and new ones keep growing in. It hunts seals.

cards.name: Hammerhead Shark
cards.def: Its wide, flat head is shaped like a hammer. The great hammerhead uses its head to pin down stingrays.

cards.name: Tiger Shark
cards.def: Young tiger sharks have dark stripes like a tiger. It eats almost anything — even tires and license plates!

cards.name: Bull Shark
cards.def: It can swim from the salty sea into freshwater rivers — one went 700 miles up the Mississippi River!

cards.name: Mako Shark
cards.def: The fastest shark in the sea! It can leap high out of the water.

cards.name: Whale Shark
cards.def: The biggest fish in the world — it can grow longer than a school bus! It eats tiny plankton.

cards.name: Basking Shark
cards.def: The second-biggest fish in the world. It has a giant mouth for catching tiny plankton.

cards.name: Blue Shark
cards.def: Its back is deep blue. It swims very far — from New England all the way to South America.

cards.name: Lemon Shark
cards.def: Its skin is yellowish, like a lemon. The color helps it hide over the sandy sea floor.

cards.name: Thresher Shark
cards.def: Its tail can be as long as its body! It whips its tail to stun the fish it eats.

cards.name: Blacktip Reef Shark
cards.def: The tips of its fins look dipped in black paint. It swims in shallow water near coral reefs.

cards.name: Leopard Shark
cards.def: It has dark spots like a leopard. It swims near the shore from Oregon down to Mexico.

cards.name: Nurse Shark
cards.def: It rests in the daytime and hunts at night on the sea floor, sucking up food like a vacuum.

cards.name: Zebra Shark
cards.def: Baby zebra sharks have stripes like a zebra, but grown-ups have spots!

cards.name: Wobbegong
cards.def: Its pattern looks like a carpet. It lies still on the sea floor and waits for fish to come close.

cards.name: Angel Shark
cards.def: It is flat like a pancake. It buries itself in the sand and waits to grab fish.

cards.name: Goblin Shark
cards.def: It lives deep in the ocean and has pink skin. Its jaws shoot forward to snatch food.

cards.name: Greenland Shark
cards.def: It swims very slowly in icy water and can live for hundreds of years — longer than any other animal with a backbone.

cards.name: Sand Tiger Shark
cards.def: It is the only shark known to gulp air at the surface and hold it in its belly, so it can float without swimming.

cards.name: Bonnethead Shark
cards.def: Its head is shaped like a shovel, and it was the first shark found to eat plants — it munches seagrass!

cards.name: Sawshark
cards.def: Its long nose is edged with teeth like a saw, and two long whiskers hang from the middle of it.

cards.name: Spiny Dogfish
cards.def: It has a sharp spine by each back fin, and it hunts in packs that can have thousands of sharks!

cards.name: Blacktip Shark
cards.def: It can leap out of the water and spin around three or four times before it splashes back down!

cards.name: Whitetip Reef Shark
cards.def: It can rest in a cave all day without swimming, then squeeze into holes in the reef to find food at night.

cards.name: Oceanic Whitetip Shark
cards.def: Its long, rounded fins have white tips, and it roams the open ocean far from land.

cards.name: Caribbean Reef Shark
cards.def: It can lie still on the sea floor or inside a cave, which is unusual for a shark that swims so much.

cards.name: Gray Reef Shark
cards.def: When it feels bothered, it hunches its back and swims in a wiggly way to warn others to stay back.

cards.name: Silky Shark
cards.def: It is named for its skin, which feels smooth like silk.

cards.name: Sandbar Shark
cards.def: It has a very tall back fin, and lots of babies grow up in Chesapeake Bay.

cards.name: Dusky Shark
cards.def: It grows very slowly and is not a grown-up until it is about 20 years old.

cards.name: Silvertip Shark
cards.def: Every one of its fins has a bright white edge, which is how it got its name.

cards.name: Galápagos Shark
cards.def: It is named after the Galápagos Islands, where the first one was found.

cards.name: Sicklefin Lemon Shark
cards.def: Babies swim in water so shallow that their back fins stick up out of the water!

cards.name: School Shark
cards.def: It travels very far — one swam from England all the way to Iceland!

cards.name: Port Jackson Shark
cards.def: Dark stripes like a harness cross its eyes, and it loves to eat spiky sea urchins.

cards.name: Horn Shark
cards.def: It has a spine like a little horn on each back fin, and it pushes itself along the bottom with its fins.

cards.name: Swell Shark
cards.def: When it is scared, it swallows water and puffs up to about twice its size!

cards.name: Epaulette Shark
cards.def: It often walks along the bottom on its fins instead of swimming!

cards.name: Bamboo Shark
cards.def: Babies have dark stripes, and it can stay alive out of the water for up to 12 hours.

cards.name: Tawny Nurse Shark
cards.def: In the daytime, two dozen or more of them may pile up together to rest inside a cave!

cards.name: Tasselled Wobbegong
cards.def: A fringe of frilly flaps around its head looks like a shaggy beard and helps it hide on the reef.

cards.name: Pajama Shark
cards.def: Its thick dark stripes look like striped pajamas, and it spends the day hiding in caves.

cards.name: Leopard Catshark
cards.def: It has leopard-like spots and rests in caves by day, then hunts near the shore at night.

cards.name: Small-Spotted Catshark
cards.def: Its eggs come in tough little cases with curly strings that hold on to seaweed.

cards.name: Coral Catshark
cards.def: Its long, thin body can wiggle into small spaces in the reef, and it hunts at night.

cards.name: Puffadder Shyshark
cards.def: When it is scared, it curls into a ring and covers its eyes with its tail!

cards.name: Draughtsboard Shark
cards.def: Its blotchy pattern looks like a checkerboard, and when it is scared it puffs up with water or air!

cards.name: Smooth Dogfish
cards.def: Instead of sharp teeth, it has rows of flat teeth for crushing crabs.

cards.name: Banded Houndshark
cards.def: Young ones have dark bands and dots that fade as they grow up.

cards.name: Necklace Carpetshark
cards.def: A wide black collar wraps around its neck like a necklace, and it has white spots.

cards.name: Crested Bullhead Shark
cards.def: It has big ridges above its eyes, like bushy eyebrows.

cards.name: Zebra Bullhead Shark
cards.def: It has stripes like a zebra, and it eats spiky sea urchins.

cards.name: Blind Shark
cards.def: It is not really blind — it shuts its eyes when it is pulled out of the water!

cards.name: Bluntnose Sixgill Shark
cards.def: Most sharks have five gill slits on each side, but this one has six!

cards.name: Broadnose Sevengill Shark
cards.def: Most sharks have five gill slits on each side, but this one has seven!

cards.name: Chain Catshark
cards.def: It has a pattern like a chain, and its skin glows in the dark deep sea.
